shortDescription: Belgium has agreed to extend negotiations to buy the nuclear utility assets owned by French power utility Engie EURONEXT:ENGI in the country to November 4.

children: Belgium has agreed to extend negotiations to buy the nuclear utility assets owned by French power utility Engie
The Belgian government and Engie announced talks over the sale in April and said at the time that they expected to close a deal by October 1.

"Given the complexity and scope of the potential transaction, additional time is needed to complete the parties' ongoing analyses and discussions," the Belgian Energy Ministry and Engie said in a joint statement.
The proposed deal would cover all nuclear activities currently owned and operated by Engie and its Electrabel unit, including the country's seven nuclear reactors, some of which have been closed.
Plans to decommission some of the closed nuclear reactors were suspended when the talks started.
Prime Minister Bart De Wever said at the time the idea behind the acquisition was to obtain "a secure, affordable and long-lasting source of energy, with less reliance upon fossil fuels".
